official_measurement_examples.name: Definitive map legal-record role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England guidance describes the local authority definitive map as the legal record of public rights of way in four main categories.

official_measurement_examples.name: Open access distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: CROW open-access rights apply to mapped open country, registered common land and specified coastal margin and are separate from public-right-of-way status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 247 separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Department for Transport guidance states a section 247 stopping-up order removes highway rights to enable approved development; planning permission alone does not extinguish the highway right.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 253 timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: A section 253 process may begin while a planning application is in progress, but the stopping-up order cannot be made until planning permission has been granted.

official_measurement_examples.name: Rights-of-way objections
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where objections to a public-right-of-way order remain, the local highway authority can submit the order to the Planning Inspectorate for determination.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 decisions scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Planning Inspectorate 2026 decisions page records individual rights-of-way order outcomes and maps and must not be treated as a national parcel-clearance dataset.

official_measurement_examples.name: Common-land consent distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate guidance distinguishes works that may fall outside section 38 restricted works from works requiring consent; common-land access controls remain separate from planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ownership separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A public right of way or open-access right is a public access right and does not itself establish ownership, development capacity or permission to build.

core_rules: a definitive-map right of way is an access right not planning permission
absence from a convenient online map is not proof no public right exists
open-access land status is distinct from public-right-of-way status
planning permission does not automatically stop up or divert a highway
a stopping-up application is not a confirmed stopping-up order
section 253 process commencement is not section 247 completion
a proposed public-path order is not a confirmed legal route change
rights-of-way order decisions must retain order date route and authority context
OS or leisure-map depiction must not silently replace the legal definitive record
common-land section 38 controls are distinct from planning permission
temporary access restriction is not permanent extinguishment of public rights
public access rights do not determine land ownership
public rights do not reserve development capacity or utility capacity
historic rights-of-way evidence must retain legal and temporal context
no parcel access clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Natural England, Department for Transport and Planning Inspectorate sources were checked on 2026-07-26. April-June 2026 rights-of-way updates and March 2026 common-land guidance were preserved as legal/access evidence, not parcel development clearance.
